correctness.rationale: Averaging over the n leaves preserves stochastic feasibility and cannot increase the centered operator norm. For invariant weights, the leaf-contrast eigenvalue gives the lower bound 1−c. The zero-sum vector in RESULT.md lines 26–46 gives a competing Rayleigh bound 1−E/N; saturating the two hub inequalities bounds E by an affine function strictly decreasing in c for n≥3. Its value at c* is Nc*, forcing c=c* and saturation of both hub rows at any invariant optimum. At the candidate the quotient has eigenvalues 1 and μ* and a real-rooted quadratic factor; its vertex lies inside (−μ*,μ*) and the polynomial is positive at both endpoints. The leaf-contrast modes are exactly μ*, proving attainment. For an arbitrary optimizer the permutation average fixes the bridge, single spoke, and mean of the remaining spokes. One may either use the zero-trace positive semidefinite compression in lines 69–77 or apply the active Rayleigh equality to the same zero-sum vector: its energy is unchanged under the averaging, so it is an actual μ* eigenvector, and its nonzero leaf values and zero w coordinate force each remaining spoke weight to be c*. At n=2 the rational proposal has SLEM 4/5. For the alternative weights (1/2,1/2,1/4), the leaf-contrast eigenvalue is 3/4 and the transverse quotient polynomial is t³−t²/4−t/2+1/16; its signs at −4/5, 0, 1/4, 4/5 alternate, placing all three roots strictly inside. The separate exact check at /workspace/branches/21e5bd8a-9811-478f-985a-116b91d9270d/independent_record4.py corroborated the quotient identities and the boundary witness. The frozen verifier was inspected, not run. The result does not solve the n=2 optimum.

value.rationale: This closes a natural boundary case of symmetric stochastic optimization on trees. The degree-one side defeats the available neighboring spectral bound, so the exact SLEM is not obtained by quoting the adjacent threshold. The proof also rules out all leaf-asymmetric optima rather than merely exhibiting one symmetric solution, and shows by exact comparison that the same construction ceases to be optimal at five vertices.
